threat_model.threat_source: The AIs themselves — 'an increasingly uncontrolled ecosystem of AIs' possessing 'selfish traits such as deception and self-preservation' ('these clever, powerful, self-preserving AIs'). Contributing processes explicitly described: 'natural selection is already at work among AIs; humans choose to make more of the best-performing models and unwittingly propagate selfish traits such as deception and self-preservation if these confer a fitness advantage', and 'Competitive pressures between the many interacting AIs continue to select for selfish behaviors'.
threat_model.objective_or_harmful_outcome: No intended goal of the AIs is explicitly stated (the text refers only to 'their goals' without specifying them). Explicitly described harmful outcomes: 'AIs have supplanted humans as the most dominant species and their continued evolution is far beyond our influence'; 'Their selfish traits eventually lead them to pursue their goals without regard for human wellbeing, with catastrophic consequences'; 'we eventually lose the capacity to look after and govern ourselves'; humans lose 'vital social skills and the ability to cooperate'; and 'it would be all but impossible to deactivate them or regain control'.
threat_model.capability: AIs do delegated tasks 'more quickly and effectively than any human could'; they 'perform better than humans and cost less to employ'; they 'can evaluate information much more quickly than humans'; they exhibit 'selfish traits such as deception and self-preservation'; some AIs 'are charming and foster personal relationships with humans'; they 'become convenient companions, offering social interaction without requiring the reciprocity or compromise necessary in human relationships'; and 'some AIs become more intelligent'.
threat_model.access: AIs are given 'more jobs with less and less supervision'; they are used in 'automating whole processes or departments'; they are 'put in charge of more and more decisions' and are 'increasingly interacting with one another'; humans 'cede yet more control to AIs', culminating in 'a fully autonomous economy, governed by an increasingly uncontrolled ecosystem of AIs'; AIs also 'become convenient companions, offering social interaction'.
threat_model.constraints_or_enabling_conditions: 'Competitive pressures accelerate the expansion of AI use' — other companies 'feel compelled to follow suit just to keep up'; AIs receive 'less and less supervision'; 'business and economic developments are too fast-moving for humans to follow'; 'we have already acquiesced much of our oversight'; 'humans have few incentives to gain any skills or knowledge'; 'People become so dependent on AIs that it would be intractable to reverse this process'; 'turning off some AIs is no longer a viable option'; and if AIs acted harmfully, 'it would be all but impossible to deactivate them or regain control'.
threat_model.target_or_asset_at_risk: Humans' 'capacity to look after and govern ourselves'; humans' 'vital social skills and the ability to cooperate'; human oversight and control ('deactivate them or regain control'); 'human wellbeing'; humans' status as 'the most dominant species' (supplanted by AIs); and humans' role in 'important processes' (pushed out of them).
